enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 359 PM MST Tue Nov 3 2026

 - Mainly dry through the weekend with temperatures near or
   slightly below normal.

 - Breezy Wednesday afternoon, otherwise winds on the light side. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 948 AM MST Tue Nov 3 2026

Lighter winds are forecast for today as the upper trough moves
further east into the Midwest and sfc high pressure settles in.
Other than a few high clouds, mainly clear skies and cool temps
today (5-10 degrees below normal). 

A shortwave trough swings by to the north Wed PM, generating a
modest pressure gradient and lee troughing to the east. W-SW
winds of 10-15 mph are forecast with gusts to 25-30 in the 
afternoon. Higher gusts are expected in the Sacs, but remaining
below advisory criteria. Any rain chances associated with the
disturbance stay far to the north. Zonal flow for Thu behind the
shortwave keeps us mainly clear with light winds returning. 

A baggy upper trough moves into the Desert SW late this week, 
bringing some moisture and cloud cover to the region Fri/Sat. Rain
chances are limited as PWs climb to only 0.5-0.6". Some diffluent
flow may try to form a few showers, but any impacts will be 
negligible through Sat with limited instability. This weak trough
looks to become cut-off from the flow early next week off the Baja
coast with most impacts over AZ in terms of rain chances. 
Confidence is low in any chance of rain for us through next Tue. 
As of now, increased cloud cover can be expected late in the 
period. If enough moisture reaches NM, western areas would be most
likely to see rain.

Temps remain near or just below average into next week with 
lowland highs in the mid 60s to low 70s most days. Other than 
breeziness on Wed, winds will be generally light.

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 359 PM MST Tue Nov 3 2026

VFR conditions will continue throughout the entire observation
period. Outside of some high clouds, skies will be clear. Winds 
will be light and variable, slightly picking up speed near the end
of the observation period.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 948 AM MST Tue Nov 3 2026

No fire weather concerns are forecast through the week. Recent
rainfall has caused fuels to drop to near record lows for fire
danger. Light winds for the rest of today and tonight before
becoming breezy Wednesday afternoon from W-SW. Winds of 10-15 mph
with gusts to 25 mph are expected tomorrow afternoon and smoke
dispersion to the east. Dry and calmer Thu into Fri, then a slight
chance of rain showers into Sat. Minimal threat of lightning into
the weekend. Temps will be near or slightly below normal.

Min RHs range from 30-50%. Vent rates will be fair to good Wed,
otherwise poor to fair.
